concurrency_primitives: goroutines, bounded channels (workers*2), sync.WaitGroup, sync.Pool, sync.RWMutex (Interner), sync/atomic, context cancellation; 4 datasets loaded in parallel (ingest/load.go), chunked parallel CSV decode with quote-parity splitter and ordered collector (ingest/pipeline.go), row-batch pipeline for GeoJSON, sharded map-reduce join index (index/index.go), 5 analyses run concurrently (analysis/analysis.go), concurrent paged HTTP fetcher (fetch/fetch.go)
design_patterns: Pipeline (ingest->index->analyze->render; channel pipeline inside ingest), Factory (ingest.Open for CSV/GeoJSON/gzip, report.NewRenderer), Strategy (ingest.Source, ParseFunc, analysis.Analysis, report.Renderer), Builder (engine.NewBuilder().DataDir().Workers().Output().Build())
questions: Do neighborhoods/blocks with more open vacant-building notices experience more violent crime; which neighborhoods should be first for coordinated demolition + public-safety investment? (Vacants x Crime)
Do liquor-licensed blocks see more crime; which license types/outlets; is it a late-night problem? (Liquor x Crime by hundred-block)
Are residents in the highest-crime neighborhoods getting slower or less reliable 311 service? (311 x Crime)
How much resident-reported blight comes from blocks with vacant buildings; is there a dose-response? (311 x Vacants by block)
Which council districts carry the heaviest combined burden for the next capital budget? (Crime x Vacants x 311 x Liquor, two-hop joins)
stakeholders: Dept. of Housing and Community Development (DHCD)
overview: Nine-package Go engine with a Source factory (CSV/GeoJSON/gzip), chunked parallel CSV decoding, sharded map-reduce join on normalized neighborhood and hundred-block keys, Strategy-based analyses returning a format-neutral report model, and terminal/plain/HTML renderers plus a token-protected local web dashboard and an optional cgo macOS app. Code is idiomatic, well-commented, tested (incl. determinism and chunked-vs-sequential equivalence), and the README matches it in detail; scope is far beyond a typical midterm.
stakeholder_value: The five questions join datasets at block and neighborhood level and produce decision-relevant findings for named agencies: a vacant-building shortlist for DHCD/BPD, a liquor-outlet watch-list with evidence that closing hours are not the lever, an honest mixed-signal 311 equity result for CitiStat, a block-level blight dose-response for DPW crews, and a four-dataset council-district scorecard with caveats. Joins are substantive (address normalization, majority-vote district assignment), not coincidental counting.
issues: Prebuilt macOS .app (second submission folder) could not be verified from the grading shell: quarantined GUI bundle produced no window or listening port; source-built equivalent and embedded UI server work.
go build ./... prints harmless ld warnings for the cgo native-app package (macOS 14.4 objects linked for 13.0 target).
Gzipped 311 ingest is single-stream DEFLATE-bound (2.0 s of 3.3 s); README documents ./run.sh unpack to remove the bottleneck.
Only 66% of 311 rows yield a block key (no address on call-center requests); documented.
Binary must be run from repo root or with -data (run.sh handles it).
rationale: All eight criteria are fully met and verified: clean build and vet, four real bundled Open Baltimore datasets, parallel parse and join with race-clean synchronization and determinism tests, measured memory design, a clean multi-package architecture realizing Factory/Strategy/Builder/Pipeline with tests, five substantive cross-dataset questions for named stakeholders with ASCII, HTML and web-UI output, and a README that matches reality. The unverifiable prebuilt .app is an extra and not deducted. 100/100, A.
